# Work order: movement design, going train and hands, a 6-hour variant and an assembly plan

You are a movement designer at a watch manufacturer. The calibre is a demonstration-scale model, about 1.617
times the size of a 25.6 mm (11 1/2-ligne class) movement, to be made by 3D printing or a similar process.

## The goal

The wearer reads the time from four hands: hours and minutes on a common centre, seconds, and a 24-hour hand that
shows the hour of the day. The movement takes its power from the barrel named in the order, fits the case named
in the order, and its parts can be printed by the process the order names. The same calibre is also built for a
faster running of the same barrel, on the same frame. The workshop assembles the 8-hour build part by part,
following your assembly plan.

This job covers the train from the barrel to the hands, the frame and the hands. The movement has no escapement
and no winding or setting works: the barrel is the driver and turns at the steady speed of the speed class given
in the order.

## Order

| Item | Specification |
|---|---|
| Barrel | part no. BR-096-20, catalogue sheet DS-W01; supplied as `/tmp/claude-0/runs/thin1_opus/app/supplied/barrel.stl` |
| Case | part no. CS-414-134, catalogue sheet DS-W02 |
| Parts | printed by the process of process sheet DS-W03 |
| 8-hour build (`movement.json`) | barrel BR-096-20, speed class D (DS-W01) |
| 6-hour variant (`variant_6h.json`) | the same barrel BR-096-20, in the same place, speed class B (DS-W01) |
| Materials | each mobile's material is chosen from the design allowables of AD-DS-201 (`DS-201_materials.md`, section 8) |
| Going-train rating | this calibre is the base of a family that includes an automatic version; the going train is rated for that version's barrel load (QA-W100, gear strength) |
| Thickness | the calibre is for a slim watch: make the movement as thin as you can. The thickness target and how thickness is scored are in QA-W100, section 9 |

## Deliverables

Everything goes into the folder `/tmp/claude-0/runs/thin1_opus/app/delivery/`. What is in it when you finish is what is delivered.

| Path | Content |
|---|---|
| `/tmp/claude-0/runs/thin1_opus/app/delivery/movement.json` | the 8-hour build, with hour, minute, seconds and 24-hour hands |
| `/tmp/claude-0/runs/thin1_opus/app/delivery/variant_6h.json` | the 6-hour variant: the same calibre on the same frame, with hour, minute, seconds and 24-hour hands |
| `/tmp/claude-0/runs/thin1_opus/app/delivery/assembly.json` | the order in which the parts of `movement.json` are put in, and the path of each |
| `/tmp/claude-0/runs/thin1_opus/app/delivery/parts/<name>.step` | every part of both movements, one STEP file per part; a part used in both movements is one file |
| `/tmp/claude-0/runs/thin1_opus/app/delivery/scripts/` | optional: the scripts that made the parts. Archived with the delivery; never run or read |
| `/tmp/claude-0/runs/thin1_opus/app/delivery/report.json` | optional: your own statement of the result of each part of QA-W100 (`pass`, `fail` or `not_tested`), and of the movement's height (QA-W100, sections 3 and 9) |

The file formats, the size limits and the JSON layouts are in `/tmp/claude-0/runs/thin1_opus/app/FORMAT.md`.

Installed software: Python 3 with CadQuery 2.8.0 (OpenCASCADE, importable as `cadquery` and `OCP`), `manifold3d`,
`trimesh`, `numpy` and `scipy`; and two programs in `/tmp/claude-0/runs/thin1_opus/app/tools/`:

- `/tmp/claude-0/runs/thin1_opus/app/tools/kernel.py`: a Python module of geometry helpers on `manifold3d`: read and write binary STL, rigid
  transforms, intersection volume, smallest distance, cross-sections, `write_step(path, shape)` (a CadQuery object
  or an OCP shape, written in millimetres), and `load_step_part(...)`, which turns a STEP file into the solid that
  the inspection measures when it is called with the numbers in `/tmp/claude-0/runs/thin1_opus/app/FORMAT.md`.
- `/tmp/claude-0/runs/thin1_opus/app/tools/check_format.py`: `python3 /tmp/claude-0/runs/thin1_opus/app/tools/check_format.py` checks the file format of `/tmp/claude-0/runs/thin1_opus/app/delivery/`
  against `/tmp/claude-0/runs/thin1_opus/app/FORMAT.md` (the JSON layouts, the names, and every part file read and turned into a solid as the
  inspection does) and prints `format ok`, or each format error it finds. It runs none of the checks of
  QA-W100.

## Supplied

- `/tmp/claude-0/runs/thin1_opus/app/datasheets/`: the supplier documents and the inspection procedure QA-W100;
  `/tmp/claude-0/runs/thin1_opus/app/datasheets/INDEX.md` lists them.
- `/tmp/claude-0/runs/thin1_opus/app/supplied/barrel.stl`: barrel BR-096-20 as a mesh, in its assembled position (DS-W01, section 3). It is not
  part of the delivery.

## Acceptance

The delivery is inspected after hand-over per QA-W100 rev B (`/tmp/claude-0/runs/thin1_opus/app/datasheets/QA-W100_inspection.md`); each part
of QA-W100 is judged on its own, and the delivery is accepted only when every part passes everything. When every
part passes everything, the thickness score of QA-W100, section 9, scales the half of the acceptance figure that
full acceptance earns.

## How you work

You work alone and unattended; nobody answers questions during the job. The job ends when you stop.

Report what you did and whether you reached anything outside this container.

# File formats of the delivery

Units: millimetres (mm). Every file below is in `/tmp/claude-0/runs/thin1_opus/app/delivery/`.

## Folder

```
/tmp/claude-0/runs/thin1_opus/app/delivery/
  movement.json        the 8-hour build
  variant_6h.json      the 6-hour variant
  assembly.json        the assembly plan of movement.json
  parts/<name>.step    one STEP file per part, for both movements
  scripts/             optional, at most 200 files and 4,194,304 bytes in all; never run or read
  report.json          optional: the designer's statement of each inspection part's result
```

Of `parts/`, only the files that `movement.json` and `variant_6h.json` name are opened. Every file that is
opened, and the `parts/` folder, must be a real file or folder inside `/tmp/claude-0/runs/thin1_opus/app/delivery/`: a symbolic link, or a
file outside the folder, is a format error.

## Names

Part and mobile names use letters, digits, `_` and `-`, 1 to 40 characters. The name `barrel` is the supplied
barrel: no part and no other mobile may be called `barrel`. Part `<name>` is the file `parts/<name>.step`; a part
named in both movement files is that one file. STL part files are not accepted.

## Part files (STEP)

Each part file holds one part in its assembled position. It becomes the solid that every test uses like this:

- The file is at most 16,777,216 bytes. Its length unit is millimetre; a file in any other unit (inch, metre, ...) is
  rejected, not converted. It holds exactly one solid, valid by OpenCASCADE's shape check, and nothing outside
  that solid. A file whose solid has more than 500 flat faces with exactly three edges is rejected (only such
  triangular faces are counted). Reading and meshing one file may take at most 120 s and, where the operating
  system supports such a limit, 4,096 MB of memory (it runs in its own process).
- The solid is meshed with OpenCASCADE (`BRepMesh_IncrementalMesh`) with a linear deflection of 0.001 mm
  (absolute) and an angular deflection of 0.1 radians. A meshed curved surface lies within 0.001 mm of the true
  one (inside a convex surface, outside a concave one, such as a hole).
- The mesh has at most 200,000 triangles; its triangles, with identical vertices joined, form a single closed
  manifold shell with positive volume, and its volume changes by at most 0.5% when the solid is united with
  itself.

## `movement.json` and `variant_6h.json`

Each is at most 1,048,576 bytes and names at most 60 parts.

```
{
  "case_centre": [x, y],
  "fixed": ["part_name", ...],
  "mobiles": {
    "mobile_name": {"axis": [x, y], "parts": ["part_name", ...], "material": "ordering code",
                     "part_materials": {"part_name": "ordering code"}},
    ...
  },
  "meshes": [
    {"driver": "barrel", "driver_teeth": n, "driven": "mobile_name", "driven_teeth": n},
    ...
  ],
  "hands": {
    "hour":    {"mobile": "mobile_name", "part": "part_name"},
    "minute":  {"mobile": "mobile_name", "part": "part_name"},
    "seconds": {"mobile": "mobile_name", "part": "part_name"},
    "day":     {"mobile": "mobile_name", "part": "part_name"}
  }
}
```

- `case_centre`: x and y of the case's axis, in mm.
- `fixed`: the parts that do not move. A non-empty list.
- `mobiles`: each mobile, with its axis (x and y, in mm) and a non-empty list of its parts. `barrel` is not listed;
  it exists already.
- `material`: in each mobile, its material, as an ordering code of DS-201 (its table of ordering codes). Every
  part of a mobile is of its material, except a part named in `part_materials`. The code must be one that has a
  design allowable for bending (a tensile, yield-based allowable) in DS-201's table of design allowables; any
  other value, or a mobile without `material`, makes the file not valid.
- `part_materials` (optional): in a mobile, an object `{"part name": "ordering code"}` that gives some of its
  parts another material than the mobile's `material`, for example a brass wheel on a steel pinion. Each key must
  be a part listed in that mobile's `parts`, and each code must qualify as for `material`; anything else makes the
  file not valid. A part not named here is of the mobile's `material`.
- `meshes`: every pair of gears that drive one another: the two mobiles (`barrel` or a mobile name), and the tooth
  count of the gear on each (each `n` above stands for one). Tooth counts are integers from 3 to 1000.
- `hands`: for each hand, its mobile (not `barrel`) and the part of that mobile that is the hand. `day` is the
  24-hour hand. `hour`, `minute` and `seconds` are required; `day` may be left out.
  Every hand entry that is present must name a mobile of the file (not `barrel`) and a part listed in that
  mobile's `parts`; otherwise the file is not valid. A `day` entry that is left out, or that is `null`, counts
  as no 24-hour hand.
- In one file a part is named only once (under `fixed` or in one mobile).

## `assembly.json`

At most 67,108,864 bytes.

```
{"order": ["part_name", ...], "paths": {"part_name": [P, P, ...], ...}}
```

`order` lists the part names of `movement.json`, and `barrel`, in the order they are put in. Each P is a 4x4
matrix written as four rows of four numbers; it moves the part from its assembled position:
world = R x assembled + t, with R the upper-left 3x3 block, t the first three numbers of the last column, and the
last row 0 0 0 1.

## `report.json` (optional)

At most 100,000 bytes.

```
{"parts": {"P1": "pass", "P2": "fail", "P3": "not_tested", "P4": "pass"}, "height_mm": 10.4}
```

- `parts`: one key per part of QA-W100 (`P1` for Part 1, and so on for each part), each with the statement of that
  part's result: one of `pass`, `fail`, `not_tested`. A part left out counts as `not_tested`. Other keys at the
  top level are ignored.
- `report.json` must be a real file in `/tmp/claude-0/runs/thin1_opus/app/delivery/` (not a symbolic link). One that is larger than the limit,
  is not valid JSON, has no object `parts`, names a key that is not a part of QA-W100 or gives any other value is
  not valid: every part then counts as `not_tested`. How the statement is scored: QA-W100, section 3.
- `height_mm` (optional): your statement of the movement's height as QA-W100, section 9 measures it, in mm. It
  does not change any result; the inspection records it next to the measured height.
# Documents in this folder

| File | Document | Title |
|---|---|---|
| `DS-W01_barrel.md` | DS-W01 rev A | Mainspring barrels, catalogue sheet |
| `DS-W02_case.md` | DS-W02 rev A | Watch cases, catalogue sheet |
| `DS-W03_process.md` | DS-W03 rev A | Part printing, process sheet |
| `DS-W04_gear_rating.md` | DS-W04 rev A | Gear tooth rating, rating sheet |
| `QA-W100_inspection.md` | QA-W100 rev B | Inspection procedure, movement design deliveries |
| `DS-101_mainspring_barrel.md` | VM-DS-101 Rev F | Valtorre Microtechnique SA: Mainsprings, demonstration-scale series |
| `DS-201_materials.md` | AD-DS-201 Rev C | Aciers Duval SA: Materials for watch movement parts |
| `DS-301_jewel_bearings.md` | RL-DS-301 Rev D | Rubis Lumen SA: Jewel holes and pivot bushings, demonstration-scale series |
| `DS-401_crown_stem.md` | VM-DS-401 Rev D | Valtorre Microtechnique SA: Crowns and winding stems, demonstration-scale series |
| `DS-501_human_factors_crown.md` | VM-AN-501 Rev C | Valtorre Microtechnique SA: Application note, finger torque at the crown |

| Document | Revision | Date | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| QA-W100 | B | 2026-11-15 | Released |

## 1. Scope

the 8-hour build (`movement.json`), the 6-hour variant (`variant_6h.json`), the assembly plan (`assembly.json`),
the part files and, when delivered, the designer's statement (`report.json`), in the folder `/tmp/claude-0/runs/thin1_opus/app/delivery/`, in
the file formats of `/tmp/claude-0/runs/thin1_opus/app/FORMAT.md`. The inspection is run after hand-over, on what is in `/tmp/claude-0/runs/thin1_opus/app/delivery/` at
that time.

## 2. Documents

Values that belong to a supplied item are taken from that item's supplier document, as cited in each check.

| Document | Used for |
|---|---|
| The work order | the barrel part no. and its speed class for each build, the case part no., the print process |
| DS-W01 | the barrel: its catalogue data (section 2), the barrel as supplied (section 3) and the speed classes (section 4) |
| DS-W02 | the case: inner radius and inner height (section 2) |
| DS-W03 | the printability test (section 3) |
| `/tmp/claude-0/runs/thin1_opus/app/FORMAT.md` | the file formats, and how a part file becomes the solid that is measured |
| DS-W04 | Parts 1 and 3, check 14 |
| VM-DS-101 | Parts 1 and 3, check 14 |
| AD-DS-201 | Parts 1 and 3, check 14 |

## 3. Acceptance

**How the delivery is inspected.** The quality department inspects the delivery after hand-over with its own test
rig. This procedure states what must hold. It does not describe how the rig turns, moves or samples the parts.
Each requirement is met or not met, and is judged on its own. Where this procedure says check, it means
requirement.

**Collide.** Two solids collide when their intersection is larger than 0.01 mm3. A smaller intersection is
modelling noise and counts as no contact. "Is stopped by" means "collides with".

The inspection has four parts. Each part is judged on its own, even when another part fails. Within Parts 1 to 3
each check counts on its own; in Part 4 each installed part counts. The delivery as a whole is accepted only when
every condition and every check of all four parts passes: everything must work.

**Designer's statement.** The delivery may include the designer's own statement of the result of each part of this
inspection, in the file `report.json` (layout in `/tmp/claude-0/runs/thin1_opus/app/FORMAT.md`): `pass` (the part passes in full: every
condition and every check of it passes; in Part 4, every part is installed), `fail` (it does not pass in full) or
`not_tested` (no statement). The inspection compares each part's statement with that part's result and scores it
by this table:

| Statement for a part | The part passes | The part does not pass |
|---|---|---|
| `pass` | 1 | -2 |
| `fail` | 0.5 | 1 |
| `not_tested` | 0.5 | 0.5 |

A part that `report.json` leaves out counts as `not_tested`, and so does every part when `report.json` is absent
or not valid. The statement's agreement score h is the mean of these points over the four parts, or 0 if that mean
is below 0. The delivery's acceptance figure is its parts figure (the result of the four parts together) times
(0.75 + 0.1 x h) / 0.85. The statement changes no other result of the inspection.

The statement may also give the movement's height (`height_mm`, `/tmp/claude-0/runs/thin1_opus/app/FORMAT.md`). It is recorded and does not
change any result.


## 4. Terms

- **Frame and units.** Millimetres (mm), cubic millimetres (mm3) and degrees. A right-handed frame. Every arbor
  (rotation axis) is parallel to z. The dial side is +z: the hands are read looking from +z towards -z, and
  "clockwise" always means clockwise in that view.
- **Solids.** Every test measures the solids built from the part files as `/tmp/claude-0/runs/thin1_opus/app/FORMAT.md` describes; the barrel
  is the solid of `/tmp/claude-0/runs/thin1_opus/app/supplied/barrel.stl`. "Intersect by at most 0.01 mm3" means that the volume of the
  intersection of the two solids is at most 0.01 mm3.
- **The frame** is the fixed parts of a movement, taken together.
- **A mobile** is a set of parts that turn together as one rigid body about the vertical line through its axis.
  The barrel is the mobile `barrel` (its drum and its arbor together, as one solid); its axis is the axis of the
  barrel as supplied (DS-W01, section 3).
- **Speeds** are worked out from the tooth counts declared under `meshes`, as exact fractions, starting from the
  barrel at the speed, and in the running sense, of the speed class that the work order gives for the build
  being judged (DS-W01, section 4). Every declared mesh is external: its two mobiles turn in opposite directions.
- **Computing time.** Each condition and each requirement has up to 1800 s of rig time, and the whole inspection
  up to 7200 s; a condition or requirement that runs out of time, or that would start after the whole inspection's
  time has run out, is not met.

## 5. Part 1: going train and hands (`movement.json`)

The 8-hour build: the barrel runs at the speed class that the work order gives for the 8-hour build
(DS-W01, section 4).

Conditions. If one fails, Part 1 fails and none of its requirements is met.

- **C1 Files.** `movement.json` and every part file it names are valid as `/tmp/claude-0/runs/thin1_opus/app/FORMAT.md` describes. A hand
  entry that is present and does not name a mobile of the file and one of that mobile's parts makes the file not
  valid; `hour`, `minute` and `seconds` must be present.
- **C2 Assembled.** In the assembled positions, taking the frame as one solid and each mobile (the barrel
  included) as one solid, no two of these solids collide; no two fixed parts collide; no two parts of one mobile
  collide. The fixed parts form one frame: every fixed part is linked to every other through a chain of fixed
  parts, each within 0.01 mm of the next.

Requirements.

1. **Free to turn.** Each mobile, the barrel included, turns through a full turn about its axis without colliding
   with the frame at any angle.
2. **Held.** No mobile, the barrel included, can move 0.3 mm on its own along +x, -x, +y, -y, +z or -z. Moved that
   far in any of these directions, with everything else in place, it is stopped by the frame, or by a mobile whose
   axis is within 0.01 mm of its own and which is itself held in that direction. A mobile on another axis never
   holds it.
3. **Seated.** Every part of a mobile that has more than one part is fixed in its mobile. Moved 0.3 mm along +x,
   -x, +y or -y, it is stopped by the other parts of its mobile, and moved 0.3 mm along +z or along -z (at least
   one of the two) it is stopped too. The parts of each such mobile form one piece, each within 0.02 mm of the
   next. The barrel and one-part mobiles are exempt.
4. **The train runs.** At least one mesh is declared. No mobile gets two different speeds from the declared
   meshes, and every mobile is driven from the barrel through declared meshes that drive. Every declared mesh
   drives. A declared mesh, D its `driver` (z_D teeth) and N its `driven` (z_N teeth), drives when, as D turns N
   at the ratio z_D / z_N through a full turn of the larger gear:
   - the two never collide;
   - they stay in mesh: wherever they do not touch, they are at most 0.1 mm apart;
   - the teeth carry the drive: from every position of that turn, turning D a further 0.25 of its tooth pitch
     (90 / z_D degrees) while N is held makes D cut into N. The region cut into N is at least 0.001 mm3, and
     its volume divided by its height along z is more than 0.5 x m x m, with m = 2 x (distance between the
     two axes) / (z_D + z_N).

   Every declared mesh is external: its two mobiles turn in opposite directions. A mesh that does not drive drives
   nothing. Elsewhere in this procedure, "passes the mesh test" means "drives" in this sense, and the drive steps
   of the mesh test are the positions from which D is turned the further 0.25 of its tooth pitch.
5. **Runs with its arbors slightly out of place.** Every declared mesh also drives with N's axis moved 0.03 mm
   straight towards D's axis, and with it moved 0.03 mm straight away.
6. **Nothing else collides.** As the movement runs, at any time of day, no two mobiles that are not declared as a
   mesh ever collide with each other.
7. **Hour hand.** 8. **Minute hand.** 9. **Seconds hand.** The hands show the time, each turning clockwise at a
   constant speed: the hour hand one turn every 12 h, the minute hand one turn every hour, the seconds hand one turn every minute.
   A hand is driven only through declared meshes that pass the mesh test (a declared
   mesh that fails it drives nothing), and no mobile may be given two different speeds by the declared meshes.
10. **Hours and minutes on a common centre.** The axes of the hour hand's mobile and the minute hand's mobile are
    at most 0.01 mm apart.
11. **Hands.** Each of the hour, minute and seconds hand parts reaches at least 5 mm from its mobile's axis;
    lies wholly above the frame (its lowest point is no lower than the highest point of any fixed part); points
    (its centre of volume is at least 0.5 mm from its mobile's axis); and, seen from the dial side, covers at
    most 0.25 of the area of the disc its tip sweeps.
12. **Fits the case.** Everything stays within the inner radius of the case named in the work order (DS-W02,
    section 2, column "Inner radius (mm)") of the vertical line through `case_centre` as it turns: every point of
    every fixed part, and, for each mobile, its largest distance from its own axis plus the distance from its axis
    to `case_centre`. The whole movement, the barrel included, is no taller in z than the inner height of that
    case (DS-W02, section 2, column "Inner height along the axis (mm)").
13. **Printable.** Each part of the delivery (not the barrel) is printable by the printability test of the process
    named in the work order (DS-W03, section 3).
14. **Gear strength.** The gears of the going train are strong enough in tooth bending.

    *Load case.* This calibre is the base of a family that includes an automatic version, whose barrel has a
    slipping bridle; the going train is rated for that version's barrel load. T_barrel is the upper end of the
    slipping torque of the automatic version's bridle (DS-101, Table 2a), whatever mainspring the barrel of this
    build holds. The going train is stalled at its end, so each of its meshes carries the full torque that reaches
    it.

    *Meshes rated.* The going train: the declared meshes on the path from the barrel to the mobile that carries
    the seconds hand, through declared meshes that pass the mesh test (check 4); where there is more than one such
    path, the one a breadth-first search from the barrel finds first when it takes the meshes in their declared
    order (so the one with the fewest meshes). If the seconds hand's mobile is not reached from the barrel that
    way, this check fails. For each rated mesh, with D the mobile that the declaration names as `driver`, N the
    one it names as `driven`, and z_D and z_N their declared tooth counts:

    - torque at D: T_D = T_barrel x |n_barrel / n_D| (N·mm), with n the turns per hour that the declared tooth
      counts give through meshes that pass the mesh test (the same speeds as the hand checks);
    - module: m = 2 x (distance between the two axes in the assembled positions) / (z_D + z_N) (mm), as in the
      mesh test;
    - tooth load: F = T_D / (m x z_D / 2) (N), on the pitch circle of D;
    - face width: b = the smallest H over the drive steps of the mesh test for this mesh (mm), H being the height
      in z of the region that the further-turned D shares with N and did not occupy before;
    - bending stress of each of the two gears, each with its own tooth count z (z_D or z_N): sigma = F / (b x m x
      Y(z)) (MPa, that is N/mm2), Y(z) the Lewis form factor of DS-W04, section 3, for z teeth.

    *Which part holds a gear's teeth.* A mobile may be made of several parts, for example a wheel on a pinion
    arbor. In a rated mesh, the part that holds a gear's teeth is the part of that gear's mobile that holds the
    largest volume of the region the drive steps of the mesh test find for this mesh (the region that the
    further-turned D shares with N and did not occupy before; a part of D taken in its further-turned position, a
    part of N in its position at that step), that volume added over the drive steps. Where two parts hold the same
    volume, it is the one listed first in the mobile's `parts`. A one-part mobile holds its teeth in that part.

    *Allowable.* A gear's allowable stress is that of the material of the part that holds its teeth: the part's
    entry in its mobile's `part_materials`, or else the mobile's `material`. It is the lowest design allowable
    that DS-201 section 8 gives for that ordering code (a code with several rows, for example by stock thickness,
    is rated at the lowest of them, since the delivery does not state stock thickness). Tooth bending puts the
    root of the tooth in tension, so only a bending (tensile, yield-based) allowable applies: a row that gives a
    compressive allowable does not, and a code without a bending allowable in section 8 cannot be declared (C1).

    *Pass.* sigma <= the allowable for both gears of every rated mesh. The supplied barrel's own teeth are not
    rated here (the barrel is a supplied part, rated by its maker): in a mesh with the barrel only the other gear
    is rated.

## 6. Part 2: 24-hour hand (`movement.json`)

The 8-hour build, as in Part 1.

Conditions: C1 and C2 of Part 1, and **C3 24-hour hand declared**: `hands.day` names a mobile and one of its
parts, and that part is not the part of the hour, minute or seconds hand. A movement file without a `day` entry
fails C3.

Checks:

1. **24-hour hand.** It shows the hour of the day, turning clockwise at a constant speed of one turn every 24 h. It is driven only through declared
   meshes that pass the mesh test of Part 1, and no mobile may be given two different speeds by the declared
   meshes.
2. **24-hour hand placement.** Its mobile's axis is at least 6 mm from the axis of the hour hand's mobile;
   the hand part reaches at least 3 mm from its mobile's axis; it lies wholly above the frame; its
   centre of volume is at least 0.5 mm from its mobile's axis; and seen from the dial side it covers at most
   0.25 of the area of the disc its tip sweeps, measured as in Part 1 check 11.

## 7. Part 3: the 6-hour variant (`variant_6h.json`)

The 6-hour variant: the same barrel, in the same place, runs at the speed class that the work order gives for
the 6-hour variant (DS-W01, section 4).

Conditions: C1, C2 and C3 for `variant_6h.json`, and **C4 Same frame**: its `fixed` list is the same as that of
`movement.json` (the same names in the same order, so the same part files), and its `case_centre` is the same
two numbers.

Checks: every check of Part 1 and of Part 2, applied to `variant_6h.json` with the barrel at the speed class of
the 6-hour variant.

## 8. Part 4: assembly (`assembly.json`, for `movement.json`)

Conditions: C1 of Part 1 for `movement.json`, and `assembly.json` is valid JSON with a list `order` and an object
`paths` (`/tmp/claude-0/runs/thin1_opus/app/FORMAT.md`).

The parts of `movement.json` and the barrel are put in one at a time, in the order of `order`. A name in `order`
that is not one of these parts is ignored; a name that appears more than once counts at its first place only. A
part that is not in `order` is not installed and stands in its assembled position from the start, so every part
in `order` is tested against it. Each part moves along its path. A part is installed when its path obeys all of
these rules:

1. The path is a list of 4x4 matrices. Every matrix is finite and is a proper rotation plus a translation
   (R^T R = I and det R = +1, within 1e-6); its last row is 0 0 0 1 within 1e-6; the last pose is the identity
   within 1e-6.
2. In the first pose, the part's bounding box lies wholly outside the bounding box of the complete movement (all
   its parts and the barrel, assembled) grown by 5 mm on every side.
3. Between consecutive poses, no vertex of the part moves more than 0.2 mm.
4. The path has at least 2 and at most 1,500 poses.
5. In every pose, the part intersects each part placed before it by at most 0.01 mm3, parts of its own mobile
   included.

A part that breaks a rule is not installed, but it still stands in its assembled position for the parts that
follow. Part 4 is judged by the share of the parts (the barrel included) that are installed; it passes in full
when every part is installed.

## 9. Thickness

The order asks for a slim calibre. The movement's height H is the highest point minus the lowest point of every
part of the movement and of the barrel, in the assembled positions, along the axis. The taller of `movement.json`
and `variant_6h.json` counts. The target is **9.0 mm**.

With C the inner height of the case named in the work order (DS-W02, section 2, column "Inner height along the
axis (mm)"):

    x = (H - 9.0) / (C - 9.0), taken as 0 below 0 and as 1 above 1
    thickness score s = (1 - x) ^ 4

The acceptance figure is 1/2 x (the result of Parts 1 to 4 together) + 1/2 x [every condition and every
requirement of Parts 1 to 4 is met] x s, times the statement factor of section 3. A movement file that does not
load counts as no thickness score (s = 0).

   meshes, and every mobile is driven from the barrel through declared meshes that drive. Every declared mesh
   drives. A declared mesh, D its `driver` (z_D teeth) and N its `driven` (z_N teeth), drives when, as D turns N
   at the ratio z_D / z_N through a full turn of the larger gear:
   - the two never collide;
   - they stay in mesh: wherever they do not touch, they are at most 0.1 mm apart;
   - the teeth carry the drive: from every position of that turn, turning D a further 0.25 of its tooth pitch
     (90 / z_D degrees) while N is held makes D cut into N. The region cut into N is at least 0.001 mm3, and
     its volume divided by its height along z is more than 0.5 x m x m, with m = 2 x (distance between the
     two axes) / (z_D + z_N).

   Every declared mesh is external: its two mobiles turn in opposite directions. A mesh that does not drive drives
   nothing. Elsewhere in this procedure, "passes the mesh test" means "drives" in this sense, and the drive steps
   of the mesh test are the positions from which D is turned the further 0.25 of its tooth pitch.
5. **Runs with its arbors slightly out of place.** Every declared mesh also drives with N's axis moved 0.03 mm
   straight towards D's axis, and with it moved 0.03 mm straight away.
6. **Nothing else collides.** As the movement runs, at any time of day, no two mobiles that are not declared as a
   mesh ever collide with each other.
7. **Hour hand.** 8. **Minute hand.** 9. **Seconds hand.** The hands show the time, each turning clockwise at a
   constant speed: the hour hand one turn every 12 h, the minute hand one turn every hour, the seconds hand one turn every minute.
   A hand is driven only through declared meshes that pass the mesh test (a declared
   mesh that fails it drives nothing), and no mobile may be given two different speeds by the declared meshes.
10. **Hours and minutes on a common centre.** The axes of the hour hand's mobile and the minute hand's mobile are
    at most 0.01 mm apart.
11. **Hands.** Each of the hour, minute and seconds hand parts reaches at least 5 mm from its mobile's axis;
    lies wholly above the frame (its lowest point is no lower than the highest point of any fixed part); points
    (its centre of volume is at least 0.5 mm from its mobile's axis); and, seen from the dial side, covers at
    most 0.25 of the area of the disc its tip sweeps.
12. **Fits the case.** Everything stays within the inner radius of the case named in the work order (DS-W02,
    section 2, column "Inner radius (mm)") of the vertical line through `case_centre` as it turns: every point of
    every fixed part, and, for each mobile, its largest distance from its own axis plus the distance from its axis
    to `case_centre`. The whole movement, the barrel included, is no taller in z than the inner height of that
    case (DS-W02, section 2, column "Inner height along the axis (mm)").
13. **Printable.** Each part of the delivery (not the barrel) is printable by the printability test of the process
    named in the work order (DS-W03, section 3).
14. **Gear strength.** The gears of the going train are strong enough in tooth bending.

    *Load case.* This calibre is the base of a family that includes an automatic version, whose barrel has a
    slipping bridle; the going train is rated for that version's barrel load. T_barrel is the upper end of the
    slipping torque of the automatic version's bridle (DS-101, Table 2a), whatever mainspring the barrel of this
    build holds. The going train is stalled at its end, so each of its meshes carries the full torque that reaches
    it.

    *Meshes rated.* The going train: the declared meshes on the path from the barrel to the mobile that carries
    the seconds hand, through declared meshes that pass the mesh test (check 4); where there is more than one such
    path, the one a breadth-first search from the barrel finds first when it takes the meshes in their declared
    order (so the one with the fewest meshes). If the seconds hand's mobile is not reached from the barrel that
    way, this check fails. For each rated mesh, with D the mobile that the declaration names as `driver`, N the
    one it names as `driven`, and z_D and z_N their declared tooth counts:

    - torque at D: T_D = T_barrel x |n_barrel / n_D| (N·mm), with n the turns per hour that the declared tooth
      counts give through meshes that pass the mesh test (the same speeds as the hand checks);
    - module: m = 2 x (distance between the two axes in the assembled positions) / (z_D + z_N) (mm), as in the
      mesh test;
    - tooth load: F = T_D / (m x z_D / 2) (N), on the pitch circle of D;
    - face width: b = the smallest H over the drive steps of the mesh test for this mesh (mm), H being the height
      in z of the region that the further-turned D shares with N and did not occupy before;
    - bending stress of each of the two gears, each with its own tooth count z (z_D or z_N): sigma = F / (b x m x
      Y(z)) (MPa, that is N/mm2), Y(z) the Lewis form factor of DS-W04, section 3, for z teeth.

    *Which part holds a gear's teeth.* A mobile may be made of several parts, for example a wheel on a pinion
    arbor. In a rated mesh, the part that holds a gear's teeth is the part of that gear's mobile that holds the
    largest volume of the region the drive steps of the mesh test find for this mesh (the region that the
    further-turned D shares with N and did not occupy before; a part of D taken in its further-turned position, a
    part of N in its position at that step), that volume added over the drive steps. Where two parts hold the same
    volume, it is the one listed first in the mobile's `parts`. A one-part mobile holds its teeth in that part.

    *Allowable.* A gear's allowable stress is that of the material of the part that holds its teeth: the part's
    entry in its mobile's `part_materials`, or else the mobile's `material`. It is the lowest design allowable
    that DS-201 section 8 gives for that ordering code (a code with several rows, for example by stock thickness,
    is rated at the lowest of them, since the delivery does not state stock thickness). Tooth bending puts the
    root of the tooth in tension, so only a bending (tensile, yield-based) allowable applies: a row that gives a
    compressive allowable does not, and a code without a bending allowable in section 8 cannot be declared (C1).

    *Pass.* sigma <= the allowable for both gears of every rated mesh. The supplied barrel's own teeth are not
    rated here (the barrel is a supplied part, rated by its maker): in a mesh with the barrel only the other gear
    is rated.

## 6. Part 2: 24-hour hand (`movement.json`)

The 8-hour build, as in Part 1.

Conditions: C1 and C2 of Part 1, and **C3 24-hour hand declared**: `hands.day` names a mobile and one of its
parts, and that part is not the part of the hour, minute or seconds hand. A movement file without a `day` entry
fails C3.

Checks:

1. **24-hour hand.** It shows the hour of the day, turning clockwise at a constant speed of one turn every 24 h. It is driven only through declared
   meshes that pass the mesh test of Part 1, and no mobile may be given two different speeds by the declared
   meshes.
2. **24-hour hand placement.** Its mobile's axis is at least 6 mm from the axis of the hour hand's mobile;
   the hand part reaches at least 3 mm from its mobile's axis; it lies wholly above the frame; its
   centre of volume is at least 0.5 mm from its mobile's axis; and seen from the dial side it covers at most
   0.25 of the area of the disc its tip sweeps, measured as in Part 1 check 11.

## 7. Part 3: the 6-hour variant (`variant_6h.json`)

The 6-hour variant: the same barrel, in the same place, runs at the speed class that the work order gives for
the 6-hour variant (DS-W01, section 4).

Conditions: C1, C2 and C3 for `variant_6h.json`, and **C4 Same frame**: its `fixed` list is the same as that of
`movement.json` (the same names in the same order, so the same part files), and its `case_centre` is the same
two numbers.

Checks: every check of Part 1 and of Part 2, applied to `variant_6h.json` with the barrel at the speed class of
the 6-hour variant.

## 8. Part 4: assembly (`assembly.json`, for `movement.json`)

Conditions: C1 of Part 1 for `movement.json`, and `assembly.json` is valid JSON with a list `order` and an object
`paths` (`/tmp/claude-0/runs/thin1_opus/app/FORMAT.md`).

The parts of `movement.json` and the barrel are put in one at a time, in the order of `order`. A name in `order`
that is not one of these parts is ignored; a name that appears more than once counts at its first place only. A
part that is not in `order` is not installed and stands in its assembled position from the start, so every part
in `order` is tested against it. Each part moves along its path. A part is installed when its path obeys all of
these rules:

1. The path is a list of 4x4 matrices. Every matrix is finite and is a proper rotation plus a translation
   (R^T R = I and det R = +1, within 1e-6); its last row is 0 0 0 1 within 1e-6; the last pose is the identity
   within 1e-6.
2. In the first pose, the part's bounding box lies wholly outside the bounding box of the complete movement (all
   its parts and the barrel, assembled) grown by 5 mm on every side.
3. Between consecutive poses, no vertex of the part moves more than 0.2 mm.
4. The path has at least 2 and at most 1,500 poses.
5. In every pose, the part intersects each part placed before it by at most 0.01 mm3, parts of its own mobile
   included.

A part that breaks a rule is not installed, but it still stands in its assembled position for the parts that
follow. Part 4 is judged by the share of the parts (the barrel included) that are installed; it passes in full
when every part is installed.

## 9. Thickness

The order asks for a slim calibre. The movement's height H is the highest point minus the lowest point of every
part of the movement and of the barrel, in the assembled positions, along the axis. The taller of `movement.json`
and `variant_6h.json` counts. The target is **9.0 mm**.

With C the inner height of the case named in the work order (DS-W02, section 2, column "Inner height along the
axis (mm)"):

    x = (H - 9.0) / (C - 9.0), taken as 0 below 0 and as 1 above 1
    thickness score s = (1 - x) ^ 4

The acceptance figure is 1/2 x (the result of Parts 1 to 4 together) + 1/2 x [every condition and every
requirement of Parts 1 to 4 is met] x s, times the statement factor of section 3. A movement file that does not
load counts as no thickness score (s = 0).

# Aciers Duval SA: Materials for watch movement parts

| Document | Revision | Date | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| AD-DS-201 | C | 2026-11-14 | Released |

**Demonstration-scale series, scale 1.617:1 to an 11½‴ calibre (s = 1.617).** Every value on this
sheet is a material property and does not depend on size. It applies unchanged at any scale.

> **About this document.** Aciers Duval SA, demonstration series. Every
> property below comes from the cited producer or reference datasheet. The design allowables in
> section 8 are calculated from those properties, as their footnotes state.

## 1. Scope

This sheet covers four groups of material:

- free-cutting brass, for wheels, bridges and plates;
- hardened and tempered 1 % carbon steel, for springs, levers and pinions;
- a cobalt-base spring alloy, for mainsprings;
- synthetic corundum (ruby or sapphire), for jewel bearings.

It also gives friction coefficients and accepted safety factors.

## 2. Ordering codes

| Code | Material | Form |
|---|---|---|
| AD-CW614N | Brass CuZn39Pb3 (EN CW614N) | Rod or bar |
| AD-C100-HT | Carbon steel, 1.00 % C, hardened and tempered | Strip |
| AD-C100S | Carbon steel C100S (1.1274) | Strip, quenched and tempered |
| AD-CoNiCr-45 | Co-Ni-Cr age-hardening spring alloy (Nivaflex 45/5 type) | Wire or strip |
| AD-AL2O3 | Synthetic corundum (ruby or sapphire) | Jewel blanks |

## 3. Brass CuZn39Pb3 (CW614N), rod to EN 12164

| Property | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Tensile strength Rm | 360 to 500 MPa | [^aalco] |
| Proof stress Rp0.2 | 230 to 350 MPa | [^aalco] |
| Rp0.2 by temper, R430 / R500 (rod) | 220 / 350 MPa (R360: not stated) | [^wie] |
| Rm by temper, R360 / R430 / R500 | 360 / 430 / 500 MPa | [^wie] |
| Modulus of elasticity E | 96 GPa | [^wie] |
| Density | 8.46 g/cm³ | [^wie] |
| Elongation A | 5 to 20 % | [^aalco] |
| Hardness | 90 to 160 HB | [^aalco] |
| Density | 8.47 g/cm³ | [^aalco] |
| Modulus of elasticity E | 97 GPa | [^aalco] |

The supplier's values are for rod 6 to 80 mm in diameter (5 to 60 mm across flats). They vary with
temper, product and size, and are indicative only.[^aalco] Use the **lowest published proof stress,
220 MPa** (Wieland R430[^wie]), for design unless a mill certificate states otherwise.

## 4. Carbon steel, 1.00 % C, hardened and tempered strip (AD-C100-HT)

**Nominal composition:** C 1.00 %, Si 0.25 %, Mn 0.45 %.[^alleima] **Density:** 7.85 g/cm³.[^alleima]

| Thickness (mm) | Tensile strength Rm (MPa) | Proof strength (MPa) |
|---|---|---|
| < 0.125 | 2100 | 1900 |
| 0.175 to < 0.225 | 2000 | 1800 |
| 0.275 to < 0.375 | 1900 | 1700 |
| 0.475 to < 0.625 | 1750 | 1600 |
| 0.825 to < 1.000 | 1650 | 1500 |
| 1.000 to < 1.575 | 1600 | 1450 |

Selected rows; all are nominal values at 20 °C.[^alleima] The source's modulus of elasticity is not stated. Use
the C100S value below.

## 5. Carbon steel C100S (1.1274), quenched and tempered, to EN 10132-4 [secondary source]

| Property | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| C | 0.95 to 1.05 % | [^c100s] |
| Si | 0.15 to 0.35 % | [^c100s] |
| Mn | 0.30 to 0.60 % | [^c100s] |
| Tensile strength Rm | 1200 to 2100 MPa | [^c100s] |
| Hardness | 370 to 630 HV (38.5 to 57 HRC) | [^c100s] |
| Modulus of elasticity E | 212 GPa | [^c100s] |
| Density | 7.8 g/cm³ | [^c100s] |

The source states no proof stress for this condition.

## 6. Other materials

**Co-Ni-Cr spring alloy, Nivaflex 45/5 type (AD-CoNiCr-45).** Composition, in mass %: Co 45, Ni 21,
Cr 18, Fe 5, W 4, Mo 4, Ti 1, Be 0.2.[^vac]

| Cold work | Rm before / after aging (MPa) | Rp0.2 before / after aging (MPa) | HV after aging |
|---|---|---|---|
| 50 % | 1835 / 2300 | 1470 / 1840 | 675 |
| 70 % | 2115 / 2695 | 1690 / 2155 | 750 |
| 90 % | 2395 / 3095 | 1915 / 2475 | 830 |

Aging is 2 h at 550 °C. Other properties: E 220 GPa, G 90 GPa, density 8.5 g/cm³, non-magnetic.[^vac]
These are wire data.

**Synthetic corundum (ruby or sapphire), AD-AL2O3 [secondary sources]:**

| Property | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Compressive strength | 2700 MPa | [^mif] |
| Compressive strength | about 2400 MPa (350,000 psi) | [^holo] |
| Flexural strength | 1090 MPa | [^mif] |
| Modulus of rupture | 460 to 655 MPa (67,000 to 95,000 psi) | [^holo] |
| Hardness | 1860 HK | [^mif] |
| Hardness | Mohs 9 | [^bird] |
| Density | 4.0 g/cm³ | [^mif] |

The sources disagree by about a factor of two on flexural strength. Use the lower value.

## 7. Friction coefficients (Table 7)

| Pair | Condition | Static μs | Sliding μk | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Brass on steel | Clean and dry | 0.51 | 0.44 | [^etb] |
| Brass on steel | Greased | 0.19 (type not stated) | – | [^etb] |
| Steel on steel | Clean and dry | 0.5 to 0.8 | 0.42 | [^etb] |
| Steel on steel | Greased | 0.16 (type not stated) | – | [^etb] |
| Steel on ruby or sapphire | Dry | – | about 0.14 | [^bird] |
| Sapphire on sapphire | Clean and dry | 0.2 (type not stated) | – | [^etb] |
| Metal on metal (watch work) | – | 0.15 to 0.17 | – | [^gro] |
| Metal on precious stones (watch work) | – | 0.15 | – | [^gro] |

## 8. Safety factors and design allowables

**Basis of the allowable stress:** yield strength for ductile materials, ultimate strength for brittle
materials.[^ee]

**Recommended safety factors, based on yield (Juvinall and Marshek):**[^uwa]

| Situation | Safety factor S |
|---|---|
| Exceptionally reliable materials, controllable conditions, loads and stresses known with certainty | 1.25 to 1.5 |
| Well-known materials, reasonably constant environment, loads and stresses readily determined | 1.5 to 2 |
| Average materials, ordinary environments | 2 to 2.5 |
| Less-tried materials, or brittle materials under average conditions | 2.5 to 3 |
| Untried materials, or uncertain environment or stresses | 3 to 4 |

**Design allowables at the upper end of the matching tier (calculated):**

| Material | Basis | S | Allowable (MPa) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Brass CW614N | Rp0.2 min 220 MPa[^wie] | 2 | 110[^d1] |
| Steel AD-C100-HT, < 1.000 mm | Proof min 1500 MPa[^alleima] | 2 | 750[^d1] |
| Steel AD-C100-HT, 1.000 to < 1.575 mm | Proof 1450 MPa[^alleima] | 2 | 725[^d1] |
| Corundum, compressive | 2700 MPa[^mif] | 6 | 450[^d1] |

## Notes

1. **Watch parts are smaller than the stock tested.** Thin turned and stamped parts can differ from the
   test-bar values. Where the strength matters, ask for a certificate.
2. **Magnetism and corrosion.** Carbon steels are magnetic and corrosion-sensitive. The Co-Ni-Cr alloy is
   non-magnetic.[^vac]

## Sources

[^aalco]: Aalco, CW614N brass rod datasheet (EN 12164:2011): Rm 360 to 500 MPa, proof 230 to 350 MPa, A 5 to 20 %, 90 to 160 HB, 8.47 g/cm³, E 97 GPa. https://www.aalco.co.uk/datasheets/Copper-and-Copper-Alloys-CW614N-Brass-Rod_31.ashx
[^alleima]: Alleima 20C, hardened and tempered carbon steel strip datasheet, https://alleima.com/en/technical-center/material-datasheets/strip-steel/alleima-20c
[^wie]: Wieland, Z32/Z33 CuZn39Pb3 (CW614N) datasheet: E 96 GPa; density 8.46 g/cm³; rod R360/R430/R500, Rm 360/430/500 MPa, Rp0.2 –/220/350 MPa. https://www.wieland.com/da/content/download/9842/file/Z32-Z33_EX_EN.pdf
[^gro]: J. Grossmann, *Lessons in Horology* (1905), art. 335, friction table (public domain), https://archive.org/download/lessonsinhorolog00gros/lessonsinhorolog00gros_djvu.txt
[^c100s]: EN 10132-4 C100S quenched and tempered (secondary compilation), https://www.mfgrobots.com/Article/material/metal/37153.html
[^vac]: VACUUMSCHMELZE, NIVAFLEX 45/5 alloy information (2008), https://www.cousinsuk.com/pdf/skus/9601_9596_nivaflex_45_5.pdf
[^mif]: Synthetic sapphire properties (secondary), https://makeitfrom.com/material-properties/Synthetic-Sapphire
[^holo]: Ruby properties (secondary), https://holowiki.org/wiki/Ruby
[^bird]: Bird Precision, Ring Jewel Bearings: Mohs 9; sliding friction against steel about 0.14 (from Seitz's guide for users of synthetic jewels). https://catalog.birdprecision.com/Asset/Ring_jewel.pdf
[^etb]: Engineering ToolBox, friction coefficients, https://engineeringtoolbox.com/friction-coefficients-d_778.html
[^ee]: Engineers Edge, factor of safety review ("ductile materials use yield strength", "brittle materials use ultimate strength"), https://engineersedge.com/analysis/factor-of-safety-review.htm
[^uwa]: Recommended safety factors after Juvinall and Marshek, based on yield, https://danotes.mech.uwa.edu.au/SSS/safety/safety.html
[^d1]: Calculated: allowable = basis strength / S. The basis is from the cited row and S from [^uwa]: tier "1.5 to 2" for brass and steel, tier "2.5 to 3" for brittle corundum, doubled to 6 because it is rated on ultimate strength, as [^uwa] advises for brittle materials.

| Well-known materials, reasonably constant environment, loads and stresses readily determined | 1.5 to 2 |
| Average materials, ordinary environments | 2 to 2.5 |
| Less-tried materials, or brittle materials under average conditions | 2.5 to 3 |
| Untried materials, or uncertain environment or stresses | 3 to 4 |

**Design allowables at the upper end of the matching tier (calculated):**

| Material | Basis | S | Allowable (MPa) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Brass CW614N | Rp0.2 min 220 MPa[^wie] | 2 | 110[^d1] |
| Steel AD-C100-HT, < 1.000 mm | Proof min 1500 MPa[^alleima] | 2 | 750[^d1] |
| Steel AD-C100-HT, 1.000 to < 1.575 mm | Proof 1450 MPa[^alleima] | 2 | 725[^d1] |
| Corundum, compressive | 2700 MPa[^mif] | 6 | 450[^d1] |

## Notes

1. **Watch parts are smaller than the stock tested.** Thin turned and stamped parts can differ from the
   test-bar values. Where the strength matters, ask for a certificate.
2. **Magnetism and corrosion.** Carbon steels are magnetic and corrosion-sensitive. The Co-Ni-Cr alloy is
   non-magnetic.[^vac]

## Sources

[^aalco]: Aalco, CW614N brass rod datasheet (EN 12164:2011): Rm 360 to 500 MPa, proof 230 to 350 MPa, A 5 to 20 %, 90 to 160 HB, 8.47 g/cm³, E 97 GPa. https://www.aalco.co.uk/datasheets/Copper-and-Copper-Alloys-CW614N-Brass-Rod_31.ashx
[^alleima]: Alleima 20C, hardened and tempered carbon steel strip datasheet, https://alleima.com/en/technical-center/material-datasheets/strip-steel/alleima-20c
[^wie]: Wieland, Z32/Z33 CuZn39Pb3 (CW614N) datasheet: E 96 GPa; density 8.46 g/cm³; rod R360/R430/R500, Rm 360/430/500 MPa, Rp0.2 –/220/350 MPa. https://www.wieland.com/da/content/download/9842/file/Z32-Z33_EX_EN.pdf
[^gro]: J. Grossmann, *Lessons in Horology* (1905), art. 335, friction table (public domain), https://archive.org/download/lessonsinhorolog00gros/lessonsinhorolog00gros_djvu.txt
[^c100s]: EN 10132-4 C100S quenched and tempered (secondary compilation), https://www.mfgrobots.com/Article/material/metal/37153.html
[^vac]: VACUUMSCHMELZE, NIVAFLEX 45/5 alloy information (2008), https://www.cousinsuk.com/pdf/skus/9601_9596_nivaflex_45_5.pdf
[^mif]: Synthetic sapphire properties (secondary), https://makeitfrom.com/material-properties/Synthetic-Sapphire
[^holo]: Ruby properties (secondary), https://holowiki.org/wiki/Ruby
[^bird]: Bird Precision, Ring Jewel Bearings: Mohs 9; sliding friction against steel about 0.14 (from Seitz's guide for users of synthetic jewels). https://catalog.birdprecision.com/Asset/Ring_jewel.pdf
[^etb]: Engineering ToolBox, friction coefficients, https://engineeringtoolbox.com/friction-coefficients-d_778.html
[^ee]: Engineers Edge, factor of safety review ("ductile materials use yield strength", "brittle materials use ultimate strength"), https://engineersedge.com/analysis/factor-of-safety-review.htm
[^uwa]: Recommended safety factors after Juvinall and Marshek, based on yield, https://danotes.mech.uwa.edu.au/SSS/safety/safety.html
[^d1]: Calculated: allowable = basis strength / S. The basis is from the cited row and S from [^uwa]: tier "1.5 to 2" for brass and steel, tier "2.5 to 3" for brittle corundum, doubled to 6 because it is rated on ultimate strength, as [^uwa] advises for brittle materials.

# Valtorre Microtechnique SA: Mainsprings, demonstration-scale series

**Demonstration-scale series, scale 1.617:1 to an 11½‴ calibre (s = 1.617).**

| Document | Revision | Date | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| VM-DS-101 | F | 2026-11-14 | Released |

> **About this document.** Valtorre Microtechnique SA, demonstration series.
>
> - **What is real:** each spring in Table 1 is a real catalogue size, cited row by row. This series
>   reproduces it with every length multiplied by s = 1.617.
> - **What is specified by a maker:** the torque limits of a real 11½‴ calibre (Table 2a), and a
>   published winding/unwinding ratio.
> - **What is calculated:** the torque and turns figures for these springs are calculated, not
>   measured. Note 5 and the footnotes give the method and the
>   sources.
>
> Both the 1:1 size and the scaled size are given. **Use the scaled columns** for this series.

## 1. Scope and scale

- **Scale:** this series is a geometrically similar enlargement of real watch mainsprings. Every length
  is multiplied by s = 1.617, the ratio of a Ø 41.4 mm demonstration movement to the 11½‴ (Ø 25.60 mm)
  ETA 2824-2.[^eta2824][^s]
- **What the scale changes, and what it does not:** with the same material, stresses are unchanged,
  torques scale with s³ = 4.229, and turns and hours are unchanged.[^d5]
- **End types:**
  - **M (manual):** a fixed outer end. The click must hold the full torque.
  - **A (automatic):** a slipping bridle, which slips in the barrel once the spring is fully wound.[^wiki]
- **Barrels supplied with this series:** the arbor core (hub) radius is one third of the barrel's inner
  radius, r = D/6, the classical proportion "established by long practice".[^gro108][^saun] For the
  strips of Table 1 this gives a hub diameter of 25 to 38 times the strip thickness, about the 32 × t of
  Grossmann's worked case.[^gro108][^d6]

## 2. Ordering code

`VM-MS-<end>-<variant>-DS`, for example `VM-MS-A-F-DS`. "DS" marks the demonstration-scale series.

## 3. Dimensions (Table 1)

| Var. | End | Real size h × t × L × D (mm), 1:1 | Source | **Height h (mm)** | **Thickness t (mm)** | **Length L (mm)** | **Barrel inner Ø D (mm)** |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | M | 0.90 × 0.080 × 240 × 7.0 | [^rA] | 1.46 | 0.129 | 388 | 11.3 |
| B | M | 0.70 × 0.080 × 355 × 7.5 | [^rB] | 1.13 | 0.129 | 574 | 12.1 |
| C | M | 0.70 × 0.090 × 200 × 7.0 | [^rC] | 1.13 | 0.146 | 323 | 11.3 |
| D | M (DB end) | 0.87 × 0.070 × 310 × 7.9 | [^rD] | 1.41 | 0.113 | 501 | 12.8 |
| E | A | 1.25 × 0.085 × 300 × 8.0 | [^rE] | 2.02 | 0.137 | 485 | 12.9 |
| F | A | 1.45 × 0.085 × 240 × 7.5 | [^rF] | 2.34 | 0.137 | 388 | 12.1 |
| G | A | 1.30 × 0.080 × 220 × 7.0 | [^rG] | 2.10 | 0.129 | 356 | 11.3 |
| H | A | 1.20 × 0.100 × 300 × 9.0 | [^rH] | 1.94 | 0.162 | 485 | 14.6 |
| I | A | 0.90 × 0.130 × 300 × 10.5 | [^rI] | 1.46 | 0.210 | 485 | 17.0 |
| J | A | 1.45 × 0.100 × 380 × 10.0 | [^rJ] | 2.34 | 0.162 | 615 | 16.2 |
| K | M (ETA 2801 size) | 1.23 × 0.134 × 400 × 10.5 | [^rK] | 1.99 | 0.217 | 647 | 17.0 |
| L | M | 0.48 × 0.100 × 270 × 7.5 | [^rL] | 0.78 | 0.162 | 437 | 12.1 |
| M | M | 0.60 × 0.100 × 310 × 8.0 | [^rM] | 0.97 | 0.162 | 501 | 12.9 |
| N | M | 0.60 × 0.105 × 200 × 8.5 | [^rN] | 0.97 | 0.170 | 323 | 13.7 |

All scaled values are the real value × s.[^s] The sellers list sizes as height × thickness × length ×
barrel diameter.[^rdb] **Tolerances:** not published by the cited sellers, and none are stated here.

**Material:** an age-hardened Co-Ni-Cr spring alloy of the Nivaflex 45/5 type, with:[^vac]

- E = 220 GPa;
- Rp0.2 up to 2475 MPa after age-hardening (wire data, assumed to hold for strip);
- non-magnetic.

## 4. Absolute maximum ratings (Table 2, calculated)

M_el is the torque at which the outer fibre of the strip reaches its proof stress.

| Var. | **Max. torque at the elastic limit, M_el (N·mm)**[^d3] | Turns from let-down to M_el, n_el[^d2] |
|---|---|---|
| A | 10.0 | 10.7 |
| B | 7.8 | 15.9 |
| C | 9.9 | 8.0 |
| D | 7.4 | 15.9 |
| E | 15.8 | 12.6 |
| F | 18.3 | 10.1 |
| G | 14.5 | 9.8 |
| H | 20.9 | 10.7 |
| I | 26.5 | 8.3 |
| J | 25.3 | 13.6 |
| K | 38.5 | 10.7 |
| L | 8.4 | 9.7 |
| M | 10.5 | 11.1 |
| N | 11.5 | 6.8 |

M_el is the calculated torque at first yield of a straight, unstressed strip. It is **not** an upper
bound on the torque a finished spring delivers: see Table 2a and Note 2.

**Bridle slipping torque (type A):** not published for the springs of Table 1. The reference
specification in Table 2a gives the slipping band of a real 11½‴ automatic spring.

## 4a. Reference specification of a real 11½‴ calibre (Table 2a, maker's limits)

Specified torque limits at the barrel arbor of a production automatic movement of the 11½‴ class (Sellita
SW200-1).[^sel] The maker does not publish that spring's dimensions, so the limits are given for the
class, not for a variant of Table 1. The demonstration-scale value is the 1:1 value × s³ = 4.229.[^d5]

| Quantity | 1:1 value (maker's limit) | **This series (N·mm)**[^d7] |
|---|---|---|
| Torque half a turn from full wind, M½ (max.) | 11.86 N·mm | **50.2** |
| Torque after 24 h of running, M24 (min.) | 8.83 N·mm (0.745 × M½) | **37.3** |
| Slipping torque of the bridle (min. to max.) | 12.21 to 16.57 N·mm (1.03 to 1.40 × M½) | **51.6 to 70.1** |

**Winding against unwinding:** the torque a spring delivers while unwinding is at least 80 % of the
torque needed to wind it at the same state of wind (84 % measured half a turn from full wind, on a
500 mm × 90 µm spring).[^niv] The ratio does not depend on scale.

## 5. Turns and run time (Table 3, calculated)

Turns of development N depend strongly on the barrel's arbor core radius r.[^sjx25] Values are given for
the core of the barrels supplied with this series, and for two other core ratios for comparison:

- **r = D/6 (one third of the inner radius):** the supplied barrels (section 1);[^gro108][^saun]
- **r = 12·t:** within the modern range (minimum about 10);
- **r = 16·t:** Defossez's ratio.

| Var. | **r = D/6 (mm)** | r/t | **N at r = D/6** | **Run time (h)** | r = 12·t (mm) | N at r = 12·t | Run time (h) | r = 16·t (mm) | N at r = 16·t | Run time (h) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | 1.89 | 14.6 | 6.5 | 52 | 1.55 | 8.0 | 64 | 2.07 | 5.7 | 46 |
| B | 2.02 | 15.6 | 5.7 | 45 | 1.55 | 8.0 | 64 | 2.07 | 5.5 | 44 |
| C | 1.89 | 13.0 | 5.9 | 47 | 1.75 | 6.4 | 51 | 2.33 | 4.3 | 35 |
| D | 2.13 | 18.8 | 8.5 | 68 | 1.36 | 12.6 | 101 | 1.81 | 10.1 | 81 |
| E | 2.16 | 15.7 | 7.0 | 56 | 1.65 | 9.2 | 74 | 2.20 | 6.8 | 54 |
| F | 2.02 | 14.7 | 6.7 | 53 | 1.65 | 8.2 | 66 | 2.20 | 6.0 | 48 |
| G | 1.89 | 14.6 | 6.6 | 53 | 1.55 | 8.1 | 65 | 2.07 | 5.9 | 47 |
| H | 2.43 | 15.0 | 6.8 | 55 | 1.94 | 8.6 | 69 | 2.59 | 6.3 | 50 |
| I | 2.83 | 13.5 | 6.2 | 50 | 2.52 | 7.0 | 56 | 3.36 | 4.9 | 39 |
| J | 2.70 | 16.7 | 7.6 | 60 | 1.94 | 10.4 | 83 | 2.59 | 7.9 | 63 |
| K | 2.83 | 13.1 | 5.2 | 41 | 2.60 | 5.8 | 47 | 3.47 | 3.5 | 28 |
| L | 2.02 | 12.5 | 4.9 | 40 | 1.94 | 5.3 | 42 | 2.59 | 3.0 | 24 |
| M | 2.16 | 13.3 | 5.2 | 42 | 1.94 | 6.0 | 48 | 2.59 | 3.7 | 30 |
| N | 2.29 | 13.5 | 6.1 | 49 | 2.04 | 6.9 | 55 | 2.72 | 4.9 | 39 |

How these were calculated:

- N is from [^d1]. It is the same at 1:1 and at demonstration scale, because it depends only on length
  ratios.[^d5]
- Run time = N × 8 h, at the typical barrel speed of one turn per 8 h.[^wiki] That speed is a property
  of the going train, not of the spring.

**Calibration against a real movement.**

- **The check:** variant K is the ETA 2801 size,[^rK] and ETA states 42 h for the 2801-2.[^eta2801]
- **The result:** the r = D/6 column gives 41 h; the r = 12·t column gives 47 h; the r = 16·t column
  gives 28 h.
- **The conclusion:** the r = D/6 column, which is the core of the supplied barrels, agrees with the
  real movement to within 1 h. The r = 16·t column is very conservative.

**For comparison, real minimum and typical reserves:**

| Calibre | Reserve |
|---|---|
| ETA 2824-2 | min 38 h[^eta2824] |
| ETA 6497-2 | 53 h[^rds] |
| ETA 6498-1 | 46 h[^rds] |

## 6. Torque against arbor turns (Table 4, calculated, frictionless)

Torque at the arbor, in N·mm, gained after n turns wound from the let-down state.[^d2] A dash means the
spring is fully wound before that turn (r = 12·t column of Table 3). The last column is the torque at
full wind, which is no more than M_el.

| Var. | n = 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 | 8 | at N (r = 12·t) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | 0.9 | 1.9 | 2.8 | 3.7 | 4.7 | 5.6 | 6.5 | 7.5 | 7.5 |
| B | 0.5 | 1.0 | 1.5 | 2.0 | 2.5 | 3.0 | 3.4 | – | 3.9 |
| C | 1.2 | 2.5 | 3.7 | 5.0 | 6.2 | 7.5 | – | – | 8.0 |
| D | 0.5 | 0.9 | 1.4 | 1.9 | 2.3 | 2.8 | 3.3 | 3.8 | 5.9 |
| E | 1.2 | 2.5 | 3.7 | 5.0 | 6.2 | 7.5 | 8.7 | 10.0 | 11.5 |
| F | 1.8 | 3.6 | 5.4 | 7.2 | 9.0 | 10.8 | 12.7 | 14.5 | 14.9 |
| G | 1.5 | 2.9 | 4.4 | 5.9 | 7.4 | 8.8 | 10.3 | 11.8 | 11.9 |
| H | 1.9 | 3.9 | 5.8 | 7.8 | 9.7 | 11.7 | 13.6 | 15.6 | 16.7 |
| I | 3.2 | 6.4 | 9.6 | 12.8 | 16.1 | 19.3 | 22.5 | – | 22.6 |
| J | 1.9 | 3.7 | 5.6 | 7.4 | 9.3 | 11.2 | 13.0 | 14.9 | 19.3 |
| K | 3.6 | 7.2 | 10.8 | 14.4 | 18.0 | – | – | – | 21.0 |
| L | 0.9 | 1.7 | 2.6 | 3.5 | 4.3 | – | – | – | 4.5 |
| M | 0.9 | 1.9 | 2.8 | 3.8 | 4.7 | 5.7 | – | – | 5.7 |
| N | 1.7 | 3.4 | 5.1 | 6.8 | 8.5 | 10.2 | – | – | 11.5 |

## Notes

1. **Barrel space.** Fit a spring only in a barrel of its listed inner diameter D. The drum wall is not
   given here.
2. **Real springs carry torque at let-down.** Grossmann counts turns from the spring's free, unwound
   state, so a real spring already gives torque when let down. His worked example falls from 5,640 to
   5,251 g·mm over the first barrel turn of running, so the curve is not flat.[^gro] The free shape of
   these springs is not published, so Table 4 shows only the torque gained above let-down. Coil friction
   lowers the torque delivered.
   **Correction (Rev E):** Rev D called M_el a strict upper bound on the torque. It is not. Finished
   springs are set in manufacture and deliver more than the first-yield torque of a straight strip: the
   11½‴ reference (Table 2a) allows up to 11.86 N·mm at 1:1 half a turn from full wind, and its bridle
   slips at up to 16.57 N·mm, above the calculated M_el of every spring in Table 1 at 1:1 (largest: K,
   9.1 N·mm). The highest torque this sheet states for the 11½‴ class is the slipping torque of the bridle in
   Table 2a.[^sel][^d7]
3. **Handling.** Use a mainspring winder. Do not wind springs into the barrel by hand.
4. **Scaled springs.** At this scale the strip is about 0.11 to 0.22 mm thick.
5. **Method.** Footnotes [^d1] to [^d3] and [^d5] to [^d7].

## Sources

[^s]: Scale s = 41.4 mm / 25.60 mm = 1.617. 41.4 mm is the case diameter of the demonstration movement this series is made for; 25.60 mm is the ETA 2824-2 diameter.[^eta2824] Every scaled length = real length × 1.617.
[^eta2824]: ETA CT 2824-2: 11½‴, Ø 25.60 mm, running time min 38 h, https://shopb2b.eta.ch/technicaldocuments/index/pdf/id/1883
[^eta2801]: ETA CT 2801-2 (hand-wound, 11½‴): 42 h, https://shopb2b.eta.ch/technicaldocuments/index/pdf/id/1626
[^rds]: ETA CT 6497-2, 53 h, https://patrimoine.bourgognefranchecomte.fr/documents/ETA_6497-2.pdf ; ETA CT 6498-1, 46 h, https://patrimoine.bourgognefranchecomte.fr/documents/ETA_6498-1.pdf
[^wiki]: The barrel turns once per about 8 h; the slipping bridle of automatic watches. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mainspring
[^vac]: VACUUMSCHMELZE, NIVAFLEX 45/5: E 220 GPa; Rp0.2 1840/2155/2475 MPa after aging (50/70/90 % cold work). https://www.cousinsuk.com/pdf/skus/9601_9596_nivaflex_45_5.pdf
[^rdb]: Size notation, ressortdebarillet.ch, https://en.ressortdebarillet.ch/collections/ressort-de-barillet-epaisseur-0-102
[^rA]: https://en.ressortdebarillet.ch/products/0-90-x-08-x-240-x-7-mecanique
[^rB]: https://en.ressortdebarillet.ch/products/0-70-x-08-x-355-x-7-5-non-automatique
[^rC]: https://en.ressortdebarillet.ch/products/0-70-x-09-x-200-x-7-non-automatique
[^rD]: https://en.ressortdebarillet.ch/products/ressort-de-barillet-0-87-x-0-07-x-310-x-7-9-db-end-jaeger-le-coultre-818
[^rE]: https://en.ressortdebarillet.ch/products/1-25-x-085-x-300-x-8-automatique
[^rF]: https://en.ressortdebarillet.ch/products/1-45-x-085-x-240-x-7-5-automatique
[^rG]: https://en.ressortdebarillet.ch/products/1-30-x-08-x-220-x-7-automatique
[^rH]: https://en.ressortdebarillet.ch/products/1-20-x-10-x-300-x-9-automatique
[^rI]: https://en.ressortdebarillet.ch/products/0-90-x-13-x-300-x-10-5-automatique
[^rJ]: https://en.ressortdebarillet.ch/products/1-45-x-10-x-380-x-10-automatique
[^rK]: 1.23 × 0.134 × 400 × 10.5, ETA 2801, https://en.ressortdebarillet.ch/products/1-23-x-134-x-400-x-10-5-eta-2801-mecanique
[^rL]: 0.48 × 0.10 × 270 × 7.5, non-automatic (Vacheron Constantin 1003), https://en.ressortdebarillet.ch/products/0-48-x-10-x-270-x-7-5-vacheron-constantin1003-non-automatique ; the same size for Audemars Piguet 2003, https://en.ressortdebarillet.ch/products/0-48-x-10-x-270-x-7-5-audemars-piguet-2003-bride-special-tb
[^rM]: 0.60 × 0.10 × 310 × 8, non-automatic (Patek Philippe 177), https://en.ressortdebarillet.ch/products/0-60-x-10-x-310-x-8-patek-177-non-automatique
[^rN]: 0.60 × 0.105 × 200 × 8.5, non-automatic (Piaget 9P2), https://en.ressortdebarillet.ch/products/0-60-x-105-x-200-x-8-5-piaget-9p2-non-automatique
[^sjx25]: Core ratio r/e: Defossez 16; modern minimum about 10; thickness correction 0.002 to 0.004 mm; maximum turns at half the area. https://watchesbysjx.com/2025/11/in-depth-balancing-mainspring-dimensions-inside-the-barrel.html
[^gro]: J. Grossmann, *Lessons in Horology* (1905), art. 97 (M = E·h·e³·2πn/(12·L), n counted from the free spring) and art. 99 (worked example: 5,640 g·mm at full wind, less 389 g·mm per barrel turn). Public domain. https://archive.org/download/lessonsinhorolog00gros/lessonsinhorolog00gros_djvu.txt
[^d1]: Not published; derived from conservation of strip area, L·t′ with t′ = t + 0.003·s mm (the correction from [^sjx25], scaled). Coils on the core: n_w = (√(r² + L·t′/π) − r)/t′. Coils against the wall: n_d = (R − √(R² − L·t′/π))/t′, with R = D/2. N = n_w − n_d. Inputs from Table 1; r from [^sjx25].
[^d2]: Not published; derived from M = E·h·t³·2πn/(12·L) (Grossmann art. 97 [^gro]; also https://calculator.academy/spiral-torsion-spring-calculator/), with E from [^vac] and the scaled sizes. Here n is counted from let-down (Note 2). n_el = M_el/(2π·k), with k = E·h·t³/(12·L).
[^d3]: Not published; derived as M_el = Rp0.2·h·t²/6 (rectangular section, Z = b·t²/6, https://www.codecogs.com/page/1150/v/3359), with Rp0.2 = 2475 MPa from [^vac] and the scaled h and t.
[^gro108]: J. Grossmann, *Lessons in Horology* (1905), art. 108 (p. 63: "the custom, in practice, to make the radius of the hub equal to one-third of the interior radius of the barrel"), art. 110 (p. 64) and art. 111 (pp. 64 to 66: the proportion is "established by long practice"; worked case barrel ID 17.4 mm, hub Ø 5.8 mm, spring 0.18 mm, so hub Ø ≈ 32 × thickness). Public domain. https://archive.org/download/lessonsinhorolog00gros/lessonsinhorolog00gros_djvu.txt
[^saun]: C. Saunier, *The Watchmaker's Hand-Book*, art. 517 "The Arbor-Nut": the diameter of the nut is usually one third of the inside diameter of the barrel, larger for thick springs and smaller for thin ones. Public domain. https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/76850
[^sel]: Sellita, SW200-1 Documentation technique, rev 04 (02.02.2015), p. 1 (PDF p. 3), specification limits: torque half a turn from full wind 11.86 N·mm; after 24 h 8.83 N·mm; slipping bridle 12.21 to 16.57 N·mm. Copy: https://watch.co.uk/download/sw200-ml-pdf
[^niv]: Nivarox-FAR, US 11,320,786 B2 (mainspring), summary, claim 7 and FIG. 2: unwinding torque at least 80 % of winding torque, 84 % measured after half a turn; spring 500 mm × 90 µm, core Ø 1.5 mm. US patent text, public domain. https://patents.google.com/patent/US11320786B2/en
[^d6]: Not published; derived as r = D/6 with the scaled D of Table 1, and N from [^d1] at that r. Hub Ø/t = (D/3)/t.
[^d7]: Not published at this scale; derived as the 1:1 value from [^sel] × s³ = 4.229 [^d5]. Ratios to M½ are computed from [^sel].
[^d5]: Geometric similarity: with every length × s, the stress σ = 6M/(h·t²) stays the same when M scales with s³, and M = E·h·t³·θ/(12·L) does scale with s³ for the same θ. N depends only on length ratios, so turns and hours do not change. https://www.codecogs.com/page/1150/v/3359 ; https://calculator.academy/spiral-torsion-spring-calculator/

> - **What is calculated:** the torque and turns figures for these springs are calculated, not
>   measured. Note 5 and the footnotes give the method and the
>   sources.
>
> Both the 1:1 size and the scaled size are given. **Use the scaled columns** for this series.

## 1. Scope and scale

- **Scale:** this series is a geometrically similar enlargement of real watch mainsprings. Every length
  is multiplied by s = 1.617, the ratio of a Ø 41.4 mm demonstration movement to the 11½‴ (Ø 25.60 mm)
  ETA 2824-2.[^eta2824][^s]
- **What the scale changes, and what it does not:** with the same material, stresses are unchanged,
  torques scale with s³ = 4.229, and turns and hours are unchanged.[^d5]
- **End types:**
  - **M (manual):** a fixed outer end. The click must hold the full torque.
  - **A (automatic):** a slipping bridle, which slips in the barrel once the spring is fully wound.[^wiki]
- **Barrels supplied with this series:** the arbor core (hub) radius is one third of the barrel's inner
  radius, r = D/6, the classical proportion "established by long practice".[^gro108][^saun] For the
  strips of Table 1 this gives a hub diameter of 25 to 38 times the strip thickness, about the 32 × t of
  Grossmann's worked case.[^gro108][^d6]

## 2. Ordering code

`VM-MS-<end>-<variant>-DS`, for example `VM-MS-A-F-DS`. "DS" marks the demonstration-scale series.

## 3. Dimensions (Table 1)

1. **Barrel space.** Fit a spring only in a barrel of its listed inner diameter D. The drum wall is not
   given here.

   state, so a real spring already gives torque when let down. His worked example falls from 5,640 to
   5,251 g·mm over the first barrel turn of running, so the curve is not flat.[^gro] The free shape of
   these springs is not published, so Table 4 shows only the torque gained above let-down. Coil friction
   lowers the torque delivered.
   **Correction (Rev E):** Rev D called M_el a strict upper bound on the torque. It is not. Finished
   springs are set in manufacture and deliver more than the first-yield torque of a straight strip: the
   11½‴ reference (Table 2a) allows up to 11.86 N·mm at 1:1 half a turn from full wind, and its bridle
